head.name: @fzlt/core/timeline
head.lead: Scripted DOM choreography on the kernel clock. Keyframe tracks animate CSS properties (transform, translate, scale, rotate, opacity, clip-path, filter, custom properties: any value whose numbers change and whose words stay) or plain numbers, with easings, delays, staggers, sequencing and overlap, labels, repeats and yoyo. Time moves in the fixed step (no allocation, no DOM); writes happen in render through the ledger, change-only, so Recall restores every property touched. Done or paused, it asks for no frames: the engine settles. With reduced motion, play() lands on the end state in one step (or build a gentler variant on tl.reduced).

blocks.label: NPM · @fzlt/core
blocks.code:
npm install @fzlt/core
import { EASES, timeline } from "@fzlt/core/timeline";

blocks.label: IN SHORT
blocks.code:
timeline(e)
  .to(cart, { translate: ["0px -150px", "0px 0px"] }, { dur: 0.7, ease: "back" })
  .label("seated")
  .to(screen, { "clip-path": ["inset(50%)", "inset(0%)"] }, { at: "seated" })
  .to(lines, { opacity: [0, 1] }, { stagger: 0.15 })
  .play(); // e.destroy() gives every property back
